what_it_does: Training AI models that help design chips requires large collections of real circuit designs as examples, but such datasets are scarce and hard to share due to proprietary restrictions. SynCircuit generates entirely synthetic but logically valid circuits automatically, creating the 'big data' that AI-assisted chip design tools need. It represents a circuit as a directed acyclic graph — a flowchart-like structure where each node is a logic operation (like AND or NOT) and edges carry signals — and uses a diffusion model (the same family of generative AI used to create images) to grow new graphs that look statistically like real circuits. A constraint-enforcement step fixes any graph that violates rules of digital logic, and a search technique called Monte Carlo tree search is used to prune away redundant logic, producing cleaner synthetic circuits. The approach is notable because earlier generative models struggled to produce circuits that were actually functionally correct.
